title: Research: Cartesian source-destination grid cost screen
body:
## Result

This is a scoped negative result for a Cartesian source-destination grid child. For block operands X_i and Y_j, the exact sparse block identity A_(i,1)=X_i, B_(1,j)=Y_j gives (AB)_(i,j)=X_iY_j for every pair. Under the generic width-r matrix-product charge, one block costs r^(2-a) size-n child units versus r^2 for separate products, so its ratio is r^(-a).

On the bounded domain r<=51 and 0<=a<=1/99, the maximum possible saving is below 5%. The exact certificate is 51*19^99 < 20^99, giving 51^(-1/99)>19/20. The first integer width reaching 5% at a=1/99 is 161. Input gathering, source access, copies, helper use, frame changes, output storage, dirty restoration, hosting, precision and interface transitions are all priced at zero in this favorable screen.

This does not construct an admissible selected-word window, establish a replacement global ceiling, exclude different bilinear algorithms, or claim a new kappa.

## Reproduction

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-cartesian-grid-screen-seed506af/verify.py` passes 15 exact formal-polynomial identity fixtures, two wrong-placement controls, exact integer threshold checks, and an integer 99th-root interval.
- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-cartesian-grid-screen-seed506af --check-only` passes source pins and package metadata.
- The registered replay launcher requires Python 3.12, which is not installed locally. The verifier passed directly under local Python 3.14.7.
